The absorber achieves perfect absorption at 1.54 μm and 6.1 μm
The emissivity in the 3~5 μm wavelength range is < 0.1
The emissivity in the 8~14 μm wavelength range is < 0.06
The absorber suppresses thermal radiation in the 3~5 μm and 8~14 μm wavelength ranges
The radiative cooling capacity of the absorber is higher than the low-emissivity coating
The absorber has a radiant exitance of 2096 W/m² in the 5~8 μm wavelength range at 500 K
The dielectric loss tangent decreases the absorptivity and increases the absorption bandwidth
The dielectric layer thickness decreases the absorptivity and increases the absorption bandwidth
The absorption spectrum at different incident angles maintains good working performance for different polarized waves at oblique incidence
The azimuthal angle has little effect on the absorption spectrum due to the good symmetry of the square element
The absorber achieves a perfect absorption peak of 99.3% at 1.54 μm
The absorber achieves a perfect absorption peak of 98.8% at 6.1 μm
The structure consists of five layers with different periods and widths
Silver is chosen as the metal material with a dielectric constant of 3.5 and loss tangent of 0.057
Polyimide is used as the dielectric material with a dielectric constant of 3.5 and loss tangent of 0.057
MgF2 is used as the dielectric material with a dielectric constant of 1.9
The thicknesses of each layer are d = 0.1 μm, d = 0.15 μm, d = 0.05 μm, d = 0.03 μm, and d = 0.027 μm
The structure is designed using CST Microwave Studio software with a finite difference time domain (FDTD) method
